data.title: Phosphoproteomic analysis identifies Grb10 as an mTORC1 substrate that negatively regulates insulin signaling
data.authors: Yu Yonghao; Yoon SO; Poulogiannis G; Yang Q; Ma XM; Villén J; Kubica N; Hoffman GR; Cantley LC; Gygi SP; Blenis J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Phosphoproteomics identify Grb10 as an mTORC1 substrate driving negative feedback on insulin/PI3K.
data.abstract_excerpt: The evolutionarily conserved serine-threonine kinase mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) plays a critical role in regulating many pathophysiological processes. Functional characterization of the mTOR signaling pathways, however, has been hampered by the paucity of known substrates. We used large-scale quantitative phosphoproteomics experiments to define the signaling networks downstream of mTORC1 and mTORC2.

extracted_findings.effect: Grb10 is an mTORC1 substrate that negatively feeds back on insulin/IGF signaling
